summary: Unlink node a2 from its current doubly-linked list and append it at the tail of this node's list. Updates the global list tail (dword_8B8F28 + 248) when a2 was the tail, and rebinds a2's owner to this.

local_names.v3: tracked tail node while walking the chain

operations.description: Read a2's previous-node link (a2[109]) and, when set, connect that node's next pointer (offset 440) to a2's next node (a2[110]).
When a2 has a next node (a2[110]), connect it back: write a2[109] into that node's previous pointer (offset 436).
If a2 is the current global list tail (dword_8B8F28 + 248), advance the global tail to a2[110] so it does not keep pointing at the unlinked node.
Check whether this list's head (this[108], offset 0x1B0) is null to choose between first-insertion and tail-walk.
Walk the next-pointer chain from the head (offset 0x1B8 per node) until the tail node is reached.
Append a2 at the tail: set the previous tail's next pointer (offset 440) to a2, or set this[108] to a2 when the list was empty.
Rebind a2: previous link to the old tail (a2[109] = v3), next link cleared (a2[110] = 0), list owner set to this (a2[107]).
Return the walk result (null when the list was empty before insertion).

unresolved: The packet fields express the global list object as *(this+0x368) while the raw source dereferences the global base dword_8B8F28 directly; the equivalence of the two bases is not fully reconciled.
Node layout semantics beyond bookkeeping (owner field a2[107], head field this[108]) are unverified.
